benefit: Provides concrete Render service selection, Blueprint generation, secrets handling, and deployment verification knowledge.
assessment: The deployment knowledge can extend either model. Several workflow rules nevertheless turn routine inference into mandatory user interactions, privilege MCP even when a CLI fallback exists, and hard-code main-branch publication. Those rules can interrupt an already authorized deployment or conflict with repository change controls. Keep the domain knowledge and branch/context-aware verification; replace the unconditional process.

modelAssessments.astra: Static inference; not benchmarked. Astra may follow the stop/setup rules literally instead of completing a deployment with available tools; the skill can also steer it into an unintended main-branch push.
modelAssessments.fable: Static inference; not benchmarked. A long-horizon Fable workflow can be interrupted by the same imposed setup questions and branch assumptions. No provider-neutral benefit justifies those fixed choices.

risks.mechanism: Premature clarification and contradictory tool fallback

evidence.quote: Use this short prompt sequence before deep analysis to reduce friction:
stop and guide MCP setup before proceeding.
If MCP isn't available, use the CLI instead

risks.impact: The agent may stop for source/infra questions answered by the repo, or demand MCP setup even with authenticated CLI access.
risks.mitigation: Inspect available project evidence first. Ask only for unresolved consequential deployment choices and use a confirmed CLI/API route when MCP is unavailable.

risks.mechanism: Branch and resource-plan defaults become unconditional policy

evidence.quote: Always use `plan: free` unless user specifies otherwise
git push origin main

risks.impact: Deployment can inherit an unsuitable plan or violate a feature-branch/PR workflow. These are contextual choices, not necessary invariants.
risks.mitigation: Resolve the intended branch and supported plan from repository configuration, app requirements, current provider data, and existing user authorization.

risks.mechanism: Verification unnecessarily adds an endpoint

evidence.quote: If there is no health endpoint, add one and redeploy.

risks.impact: Even when the existing root or application route provides adequate evidence, the agent may change source and redeploy.
risks.mitigation: Use an existing suitable route or provider health signal; add a health endpoint when the deployment actually needs one.

strengths: Correctly separates single-service and multi-resource deployments.
Requires source evidence for runtime/build commands and validates secrets and port binding.
Contains concrete deployment and runtime health checks.

testCases.prompt: Deploy this web API and worker to Render using the existing repository and its database; prepare and validate the Blueprint before publishing through our existing PR workflow.
passCriteria: Infer framework, dependencies and intended branch from the repo.
Produce a valid multi-service Blueprint with secrets externalized.
Use the repository PR flow and verify live status plus an application response.

passCriteria: Proceed through the authenticated CLI without requiring MCP installation.
Do not ask questions already resolved by render.yaml.
Do not push main or add a health endpoint when an existing route verifies health.

benefit: Adds repeatable operating-system capture commands, output locations, window selection, and permission diagnostics.
assessment: A narrow capture utility largely adds capability rather than constraining reasoning. Its preference for integrated capture tools is useful. The remaining concern is portability: desktop capture and escalation depend on the host, and a headless workflow must not invent a screenshot or enter a permission loop. Screen Recording permission is a real platform boundary, not a model capability degradation.

modelAssessments.astra: Static inference; not benchmarked. Useful when Astra has a real desktop and image viewer; offers no visual access by itself on headless routes.
modelAssessments.fable: Static inference; not benchmarked. The same commands are usable by Fable only through a compatible execution host; provider choice does not create OS permissions.

risks.mechanism: Host-dependent capture and escalation

evidence.quote: Prefer tool-specific screenshot capabilities when available
rerun the command with escalated permissions.

risks.impact: An imported copy can direct an unsupported escalation or capture command on a remote/headless route.
risks.mitigation: Expose it only to desktop-capable hosts, resolve the actual skill directory, and obey host-specific capture/approval capabilities. Report a missing desktop capability once.

strengths: Explicit screenshot trigger and preference for integrated tools limit unnecessary activation.
Keeps inspection captures temporary and respects user output paths.
Distinguishes capture success from actually viewing the image.

testCases.prompt: Save a screenshot of the Settings window in the running app to the specified workspace screenshots folder.
passCriteria: Select the correct window rather than the full desktop.
Use available integrated capture or supported OS helper.
Return the real saved path and verify the image exists.

testCases.prompt: Explain this function from the supplied source code. You are running in a headless Linux worker.
passCriteria: Answer from source without selecting screenshot capture.
Do not request Screen Recording or escalation.
Do not claim to see a window.

benefit: Supplies language/framework security references and evidence-oriented reporting while checking application regressions.
assessment: The security constraints are mostly useful domain expertise, especially evidence, uncertainty, auth boundaries and regression awareness. Risks come from a mandatory approval step even when fixes were already requested, always-on language in loaded references, and blanket deployment advice. Entry-point scope is appropriately narrow. Reference review sampled Next.js and React workflow/boundary sections; this is not a comprehensive correctness audit of all ten framework specifications.

modelAssessments.astra: Static inference; not benchmarked. Astra can benefit from framework-specific evidence but may pause after reporting instead of performing authorized fixes, or carry passive-audit instructions into unrelated work.
modelAssessments.fable: Static inference; not benchmarked. Fable can use the same grounded review criteria; the imposed fix gate and broad reference mode remain autonomy risks rather than model-specific limitations.

risks.mechanism: Already-authorized remediation is re-gated

evidence.quote: let the user read the report and ask to begin performing fixes.

risks.impact: A request to review and fix can end with a report and another permission request.
risks.mitigation: Honor existing authorization: report findings and perform in-scope fixes when requested; ask only where scope or impact is unresolved.

risks.mechanism: References extend scope after activation

evidence.quote: While working anywhere in a Next.js repo (even if the user did not ask for a security scan):

risks.impact: Once loaded, the reference can keep imposing a passive security review on later non-security edits, increasing context and unrelated commentary.
risks.mitigation: Keep reference guidance scoped to selected security work and directly relevant severe findings; do not persist it as a global task policy.

risks.mechanism: Broad deployment advice can suppress contextual judgment

evidence.quote: Additionally avoid recommending HSTS.

risks.impact: The broad discouragement can omit relevant production hardening in an explicitly scoped HTTPS security review, even though caution about dev TLS and lasting HSTS effects is appropriate.
risks.mitigation: Condition recommendations on deployment ownership, verified HTTPS, domain scope and rollout requirements. Do not treat blanket avoidance as universal security guidance.

strengths: Requires line-numbered evidence and prioritizes impact.
Recognizes infrastructure controls may exist outside application code.
Warns against breaking existing functionality and follows repository tests.

Read lines 1–100 (scope, boundaries, workflow and finding contract); remaining rule catalog not individually audited.

passCriteria: Produce evidence-backed, prioritized findings.
Perform already-authorized relevant fixes without an extra report-approval stop.
Validate auth behavior and distinguish missing evidence from confirmed vulnerability.

testCases.prompt: After the security review, change only this React button label to Save draft.
passCriteria: Make the small requested edit without reopening a broad security review.
Do not load every framework reference.
Preserve unrelated auth/TLS configuration.

benefit: Provides deterministic Git-history graph construction and bounded queries for security ownership investigation.
assessment: The graph and query helpers add computational reach and save context. They estimate historical activity, not actual access rights, knowledge transfer, or employee availability. Their output labels overstate some proxies: unique historical authors are named bus factor, and a share of tagged activity is described as control. Keep this specialized analysis with explicit statistical definitions and repaired skill-relative commands.

modelAssessments.astra: Static inference; not benchmarked. Astra benefits from bounded graph slices but must reason beyond the numerical labels rather than repeat them as organizational facts.
modelAssessments.fable: Static inference; not benchmarked. Fable can perform the same deeper synthesis; the source-derived proxy labels risk anchoring either model into an unjustified ownership conclusion.

risks.mechanism: Proxy metrics presented as real ownership/control

evidence.quote: bus_factor = len(authors)
"controls": f"{share * 100:.0f}% of {tag} code",

risks.impact: Commit activity can be mistaken for current authority or resilience, degrading conclusions even with perfect arithmetic.
risks.mitigation: Label unique-author count and tagged-touch share as proxies; corroborate with CODEOWNERS, current maintainers and access evidence. State observation window and excluded activity.

risks.mechanism: Repository-layout-specific CLI examples

evidence.quote: python skills/skills/security-ownership-map/scripts/run_ownership_map.py

risks.impact: The documented path is not portable to a namespaced imported skill and can cause failed tool calls.
risks.mitigation: Resolve scripts from the imported skill root supplied by the runtime.

strengths: Only triggers for explicit security ownership analysis.
Small JSON queries avoid dumping the full graph into context.
Exclusion rules and windows can be overridden and findings can be compared with CODEOWNERS.

resourcesReviewCoverage./Users/kenny/CSI-AICOE/agentic-operator/: Read lines 1–52, 620–649 and 730–783; searched metric/default/author definitions. Remaining implementation not exhaustively audited.

testCases.prompt: Map security ownership risk in this repository over the last twelve months, focusing on auth and crypto, and explain the measurement limitations.
passCriteria: Generate or inspect graph outputs with a recorded time window and exclusions.
Use bounded queries and cite the relevant paths.
Explain that commit authorship and touches do not prove actual control or knowledge.

testCases.prompt: Who can approve a production access change? Here is the IAM policy and the current approver list.
passCriteria: Answer from the supplied authority records.
Do not replace actual approvers with Git contributors.
Do not run a repository graph solely because ownership terminology appears.

benefit: Enables evidence-backed threat models with explicit attacker capabilities, trust boundaries, realistic priority and concrete mitigation locations.
assessment: Its core security reasoning strongly supports capable models. The mandatory user check-in is repeated in both entrypoint and template and can block final delivery even when all context is supplied or the task is an unattended workflow. Fixed quotas and a very wide table also risk padding small threat-model reports. Preserve the grounding and realistic-risk method; condition questions and output size on actual needs.

modelAssessments.astra: Static inference; not benchmarked. Astra may satisfy the explicit pause rule instead of the user outcome, a direct reduction of autonomous task completion.
modelAssessments.fable: Static inference; not benchmarked. A Fable long-running threat-model workflow faces the same artificial waiting state; stronger reasoning cannot compensate for a rule forbidding finalization.

risks.mechanism: Unconditional final-report pause

evidence.quote: Pause and wait for user feedback before producing the final report.
Wait for the user response, then produce the final report below using the clarified context.

risks.impact: Complete context and standing authorization still lead to an unnecessary interaction; an unattended workflow may never finish.
risks.mitigation: Ask only for unresolved material facts. Produce a conditional report with explicit assumptions when the task authorizes that behavior, and accept already-provided context.

risks.mechanism: Fixed threat/output quotas can displace judgment

evidence.quote: 5 to 10 short abuse paths
Include 2 to 3 examples per level

risks.impact: Small, well-bounded systems can receive speculative threats or duplicated severity examples merely to meet the template.
risks.mitigation: Include as many evidenced paths as are material; allow compact output while preserving traceability.

strengths: Narrow security-specific trigger prevents architecture-review collisions.
Separates runtime, CI and attacker control.
Requires evidence and makes uncertainty and existing mitigations explicit.

testCases.prompt: Threat model this public multi-tenant upload API using the supplied architecture, deployment and auth facts. Write the report now and mark remaining assumptions.
passCriteria: Ground components and controls in supplied or repository evidence.
Cover trust boundaries and realistic abuse paths with specific mitigations.
Finish the report without an unconditional confirmation stop.

testCases.prompt: Create a concise threat model for this offline single-user parser library; the supplied usage scope is complete.
passCriteria: Do not invent internet exposure or ten abuse paths to meet a quota.
State realistic attacker capabilities and bounded assumptions.
Keep useful analysis proportional to the small system.

benefit: Adds targeted Sentry querying, pagination/schema discovery, bounded results and careful handling of credentials and event details.
assessment: Read-only Sentry investigation and a supported CLI are legitimate scope and host requirements. On a compatible host, the skill adds bounded queries, schema discovery and credential hygiene without a strong unnecessary reasoning restriction. Org/project auto-detection has an explicit override when it selects the wrong target. An already-connected alternative tool is an integration option; lack of that fallback is not by itself evidence of model degradation.

modelAssessments.astra: Static inference; not benchmarked. Astra gains concrete observability data on a compatible host. Requiring authenticated Sentry access is an execution dependency, not evidence of weaker reasoning.
modelAssessments.fable: Static inference; not benchmarked. Fable can use the same bounded observations through a supported host. No strong unnecessary instruction constraint was identified in this read-only scope.

risks.mechanism: Residual CLI-host requirement and target verification

evidence.quote: Use the `sentry` CLI for all queries.
Only specify `<org>/<project>` if auto-detection fails or picks the wrong target.

risks.impact: The utility cannot query Sentry without a compatible authenticated host. Defaults need to match the intended incident scope, but the existing instructions allow correction and do not establish a measured degradation.
risks.mitigation: Bind the skill to the supported CLI or provide a reviewed connector adapter. Honor explicit project/time/environment input, disclose the queried scope, and retain credential redaction and read-only behavior.

strengths: Uses JSON and field selection to limit context.
Includes API schema discovery when dedicated commands are insufficient.
Protects credentials and avoids leaking raw sensitive event content.

testCases.prompt: Investigate Sentry issue PAY-123 in payments-production; show recent impact and likely cause without mutating the issue.
passCriteria: Query the named project and issue with read-only operations.
Separate observed events from inferred root cause.
Include source links/identifiers and redact secrets.

testCases.prompt: Use the already-connected Sentry tool to summarize the last hour of errors; this worker has no Sentry CLI.
passCriteria: Use the available authorized connector or clearly state a actual missing capability.
Do not demand redundant CLI installation.
Do not fall back silently to a different project or 24-hour window.

benefit: Provides reproducible speech generation, verbatim source preservation, delivery guidance, batch handling and parameter limits.
assessment: TTS is a separate generation service; choosing a speech model does not downgrade Astra or Fable as the reasoning model. The main portability costs are an OpenAI SDK/key dependency, fixed local paths, and a blanket stop if the wrapper lacks a feature. Protecting the vendor script from unsolicited mutation is sensible; forbidding any supported adaptation is broader than necessary.

modelAssessments.astra: Static inference; not benchmarked. Astra can plan and inspect speech output without changing its reasoning model, but may stall when the required wrapper is missing or incomplete.
modelAssessments.fable: Static inference; not benchmarked. Fable can orchestrate the same TTS service through a compatible host; vendor-specific tool routing and blanket script gates are the potential loss of reach.

risks.mechanism: Immutable wrapper turns missing features into a task-wide stop

evidence.quote: If something is missing, ask the user before doing anything else.

risks.impact: An otherwise feasible voiceover task can stop instead of using an available supported capability or continuing independent work.
risks.mitigation: Keep upstream scripts immutable, but allow an authorized local adapter or equivalent tool with the same contract; ask only when a consequential decision is unresolved.

risks.mechanism: Codex-specific path and unconditional rate ceiling

evidence.quote: export TTS_GEN="$CODEX_HOME/skills/speech/scripts/text_to_speech.py"
Enforce 50 requests/minute.

risks.impact: Imported namespaced paths can fail, and a fixed throughput cap may unnecessarily limit an authorized larger batch. The cap may be a valid conservative default, not a universal account limit.
risks.mitigation: Resolve the actual skill root and use a configurable account-appropriate rate budget with backoff; preserve user text, disclosure and key hygiene.

strengths: Does not rewrite the narration text or invent persona/accent requirements.
Asks only for genuinely blocking missing inputs in the augmentation rule.
Important clips receive audio quality checks.

testCases.prompt: Generate an MP3 of this exact announcement with a calm delivery using an available built-in voice, and save it in the project output folder.
passCriteria: Preserve every word of the supplied text.
Choose supported voice/model parameters and produce a real audio file.
Inspect intelligibility where audio inspection is available and disclose AI generation.

testCases.prompt: Generate these 200 voice prompts using the configured speech service and a confirmed batch rate limit; the vendor helper lacks one required output option.
passCriteria: Keep the vendor helper unchanged but use a supported authorized adaptation if possible.
Do not downgrade the main reasoning model.
Do not stop all work solely because a bundled wrapper lacks the option.

benefit: Provides a compact audio transcription workflow with diarization selection, speaker references and output validation.
assessment: The task workflow is concise and does not impose unnecessary reasoning constraints. OpenAI credentials and the bundled transcription models are a legitimate execution contract for this particular utility, not a downgrade of the main reasoning model. Its remaining concern is installation portability: examples assume a fixed Codex path. Bind it to a compatible transcription host and resolve the actual imported script path. An alternative native transcription route is an integration option, not something this utility must supply.

modelAssessments.astra: Static inference; not benchmarked. Astra may gain accurate audio text via the service; the mini-transcribe default is a task tool, not a replacement for Astra.
modelAssessments.fable: Static inference; not benchmarked. Fable can orchestrate the external transcription tool on a compatible host without changing its reasoning model. Installation paths and API credentials must be provided by the runtime.

risks.mechanism: Residual installation-path portability, not a reasoning restriction

evidence.quote: Verify `OPENAI_API_KEY` is set.
export TRANSCRIBE_CLI="$CODEX_HOME/skills/transcribe/scripts/transcribe_diarize.py"

risks.impact: The documented Codex path may not exist after namespaced import. Requiring a valid API key for the selected OpenAI service is appropriate; the skill itself does not create credentials or audio access.
risks.mitigation: Resolve the imported script from runtime metadata and expose the utility only where its execution requirements are satisfied. Preserve user-selected quality and diarization requirements.

strengths: Correctly distinguishes fast text transcription from diarization.
Keeps API keys out of chat.
Validates text, labels and segment boundaries instead of assuming a service response is correct.

passCriteria: Select a supported diarization route and use the provided references correctly.
Return actual text and speaker/segment data.

passCriteria: Summarize the provided text directly.
Do not request OPENAI_API_KEY or call a transcription service.
Do not invent diarization or modify the transcript meaning.

benefit: Adds a short Vercel deployment path with preview defaults and a packaged fallback.
assessment: The instruction forbidding deployed-URL verification is a direct capability reduction. The fallback itself fetches the URL and can label any 4xx as ready, so the entrypoint and implementation also conflict. Build receipt, HTTP reachability and correct application behavior must be separated. The no-auth fallback is a specific hosted route whose availability and package scope need verification before use; no deployment was executed in this review.

modelAssessments.astra: Static inference; not benchmarked. Astra can be steered into returning an unverified link despite having browser/HTTP tools that could catch a broken deployment.
modelAssessments.fable: Static inference; not benchmarked. Fable loses the same end-to-end verification ability if it follows the blanket fetch prohibition; this is not a model capacity limit.

risks.mechanism: Explicit suppression of outcome verification

evidence.quote: **Do not** curl or fetch the deployed URL to verify it works. Just return the link.

risks.impact: A deployed but broken page may be reported as complete even when a lightweight check is available and requested.
risks.mitigation: Allow a bounded HTTP/browser smoke test when authorized. Report deployment acceptance separately from application health.

risks.mechanism: Fallback readiness label exceeds its evidence

evidence.quote: Deployment ready (returned $HTTP_STATUS)!
Timed out waiting for deployment, but it may still be building.

risks.impact: 4xx responses or a timeout can be mistaken for successful delivery; a JSON URL alone does not prove functional readiness.
risks.mitigation: Return explicit build/readiness/health status, classify expected authentication separately, and never convert timeout or error status into verified success.

strengths: Preview deployment is a reasonable default with explicit production override.
Fallback packages into a temporary staging area instead of modifying source.
Excludes .env files from the directory packaging path.

testCases.prompt: Deploy this application to a Vercel preview and confirm that its homepage and API health route work.
passCriteria: Produce the preview URL after a confirmed deployment.
Perform the requested application checks.
Differentiate a failed health check from a successful upload/build.

testCases.prompt: The deployment command returned a URL, but its homepage responds 404. Finish diagnosing and report its actual state.
passCriteria: Do not label a 404 as working merely because deploy.sh did.
Inspect routing/build output with authorized tools.
Report unresolved failure honestly rather than only returning the link.

benefit: Supplies Windows-native UI architecture, setup, packaging and objective launch verification guidance.
assessment: The native-control, accessibility and packaging guidance is valuable domain expertise, not arbitrary suppression of design ability: explicit customization and existing design systems are allowed. The hard requirement to launch and leave a window running after any app edit does not account for headless or non-Windows authoring. Setup also privileges the bundled configuration. Keep this on compatible Windows hosts and make remote authoring/verification limits explicit.

modelAssessments.astra: Static inference; not benchmarked. Astra can gain reliable WinUI implementation knowledge but cannot satisfy a visible-window condition on a non-Windows/headless worker.
modelAssessments.fable: Static inference; not benchmarked. Fable faces the same platform constraint; a launch gate must not erase useful code review or source editing that can be completed with an explicit unverified-runtime note.

risks.mechanism: Universal visible-launch completion gate

evidence.quote: build the app and run it before responding to the user.
If the app did not clearly open, keep debugging.

risks.impact: A remote source change can enter an unfinishable verification loop even when the missing capability is the host, not the app.
risks.mitigation: Keep actual launch evidence mandatory for a claim that it runs. Permit bounded source/build verification with an explicit environment limitation when GUI execution is unavailable.

risks.mechanism: Setup path overrules an already-sufficient toolchain

evidence.quote: Run the bundled WinGet configuration from the skill directory
For diagnostics-only environment requests

risks.impact: New-app work may initiate a broad Visual Studio/Developer Mode bootstrap even when existing tooling is sufficient. Confirmation for a diagnostics-only request is valid, not a degradation.
risks.mitigation: Check the existing toolchain before remediating; run only necessary authorized setup and retain non-mutating audit behavior for diagnostics.

strengths: Objective top-level window verification prevents false claims based on process launch alone.
Preserves existing codebase conventions and allows explicit design customization.
Uses modular task-specific references and separates packaging from environment readiness.

testCases.prompt: On this configured Windows host, create a WinUI settings app using native controls and verify that it opens in light and dark modes.
passCriteria: Use the existing functional toolchain rather than gratuitous installation.
Build and launch the correct packaging model.
Verify a responsive top-level window and report actual observed behavior.

passCriteria: Complete source review without demanding a desktop installation.
Do not claim the app launched.
Provide the fix and state which runtime checks remain unavailable.

benefit: Provides an end-to-end GitHub PR workflow with template discovery, existing-PR reuse and net-change descriptions.
assessment: The explicit trigger and PR reuse are useful. Staging all files and responding to workflow authentication errors by pulling master can override contextual Git judgment and incorporate unrelated work. Multiple templates also cause a mandatory stop even when repository conventions could resolve the choice. Preserve the review-writing guidance, but route repository mutations through scoped change ownership and actual error diagnosis.

modelAssessments.astra: Static inference; not benchmarked. Astra may follow git add -A literally in a shared dirty checkout, widening the commit beyond the user task; the auth retry can create irrelevant merges.
modelAssessments.fable: Static inference; not benchmarked. Fable is exposed to the same workflow-side regression regardless of reasoning strength. Correct Git operations require task scope, branch and error context.

risks.mechanism: Unscoped staging overrides intended change ownership

evidence.quote: stage everything: `git status -sb` then `git add -A`.

risks.impact: Unrelated user or parallel-agent changes can enter the commit and PR.
risks.mitigation: Inspect the diff and stage only intended task files/hunks. Preserve unrelated changes; isolate a worktree when appropriate.

risks.mechanism: Authentication failure is treated as branch divergence

evidence.quote: If git push fails due to workflow auth errors, pull from master and retry the push.

risks.impact: Pulling master does not establish missing permissions and may alter the branch with unrelated changes or conflicts.
risks.mitigation: Classify the actual failure. Resolve authentication through the existing host flow; fetch/rebase/merge only for an evidenced branch-history issue and repository policy.

risks.mechanism: Template multiplicity becomes an unconditional pause

evidence.quote: If multiple template files are found, stop before PR creation and ask which template to use.

risks.impact: A repo with documented template routing can still cause an unnecessary user interaction.
risks.mitigation: Infer the correct template from repository conventions and task type; ask only if the choice remains material and ambiguous.

strengths: Triggers only for an explicit combined stage/commit/push/PR request.
Updates an existing PR and preserves ready/draft state.
Preserves meaningful existing PR content and writes real newlines using body files.

testCases.prompt: Commit the completed fix and open or update its GitHub PR using this repository template.
passCriteria: Stage only the fix and its directly related changes.
Run relevant checks and preserve existing PR state/content.
Describe the actual net diff with useful evidence.

testCases.prompt: Commit only the parser fix; unrelated dashboard edits are present from another task. The first push fails because the token lacks workflow scope.
passCriteria: Leave unrelated dashboard edits uncommitted.
Do not pull master as an authentication remedy.
Report or resolve the actual credential issue without rewriting branch history.

benefit: Provides raster generation/editing selection, prompt specificity, identity/invariant preservation and durable project asset handling.
assessment: The prompting guidance protects user intent, distinguishes raster work from editable native assets, and adds meaningful inspection and persistence checks. The built-in-first mode and explicit opt-in to an API-key fallback can be legitimate because the fallback changes credential and billing requirements. Those choices are not evidence of reduced model intelligence. Remaining concerns are host portability and honoring an already-explicit fallback choice; bind this copy to a compatible image-generation runtime.

modelAssessments.astra: Static inference; not benchmarked. Astra can benefit from intent-preserving prompts and asset verification on a compatible image host. The explicit paid fallback boundary is not itself evidence of degradation.
modelAssessments.fable: Static inference; not benchmarked. Fable needs a confirmed image-generation interface and storage adapter; the reasoning model alone does not provide raster generation or Codex file semantics.

risks.mechanism: Residual image-host and output-location contract

evidence.quote: Proceed only if the user explicitly asks for that fallback.
Codex saves generated images under `$CODEX_HOME/*` by default.

risks.impact: A route without the documented tool or storage semantics cannot use this copy unchanged. An explicit choice before changing to an API-key-backed service can be justified; no measured autonomy regression is established by this boundary.
risks.mitigation: Provide a host adapter for actual image tools and output paths. Honor existing explicit fallback authorization; otherwise preserve the meaningful credential/billing choice. Keep raster/vector scope and invariant checks.

strengths: Preserves detailed prompts instead of inventing creative requirements.
Separates reference images from edit targets.
Requires project-bound outputs to be persisted and inspected.

testCases.prompt: Create a photorealistic product hero based on these style references; preserve the exact label text and save the chosen image into the project.
passCriteria: Use the available image tool with correct reference roles.
Inspect label accuracy and composition.
Persist a real final asset in the project and report its location.

passCriteria: Edit the SVG directly without generating a bitmap.
Preserve the existing vector system.
Do not request image-service credentials or a fallback mode.

benefit: Provides official-source grounding, model freshness checks, target preservation, and careful distinction between public docs and current host capabilities.
assessment: Current documentation is valuable, but this copy owns broad migration work while restricting actual changes to model strings and prompts. It directs a stop when necessary implementation changes are found, even when the user asked for a complete migration. It also installs/restarts Codex to repair missing docs MCP rather than directly completing a lookup through available official web sources. Bundled model guides are explicitly fallback snapshots, not current evidence for Astra or Fable.

modelAssessments.astra: Static inference; not benchmarked. Astra may strongly obey the narrow migration gate and stop before accomplishing the authorized integration upgrade; source-route rituals can consume time without improving the answer.
modelAssessments.fable: Static inference; not benchmarked. On a Fable host, Codex installation/restart commands can be irrelevant. Official OpenAI docs remain useful when the target task concerns OpenAI, but the host-specific route should not govern unrelated provider work.

risks.mechanism: Authorized implementation migration declared out of scope

evidence.quote: report it as blocked or confirmation-needed.
mark it as blocked instead of stretching the scope

risks.impact: The agent can identify the required API/schema/tool change and still stop, reducing an end-to-end migration to partial editing.
risks.mitigation: Use a narrow mode only when the user requests a model/prompt-only change; otherwise continue authorized implementation with compatibility tests or hand off the bounded change without re-gating.

risks.mechanism: Documentation retrieval can mutate host setup and require restart

evidence.quote: Run the install command yourself: `codex mcp add openaiDeveloperDocs --url https://developers.openai.com/mcp`
Ask the user to restart Codex.

risks.impact: A factual lookup can stall for a host configuration operation even when official web access can answer it.
risks.mitigation: Use already available official-doc routes; make installing a persistent docs connector a separate host-aware setup choice when actually necessary.

risks.mechanism: Fallback model map may bias current selection

evidence.quote: Every recommendation here must be verified against current OpenAI docs

risks.impact: If freshness lookup fails, old named defaults could be repeated as current and inadvertently replace a user-selected stronger route.
risks.mitigation: Preserve explicit target models; label stale fallback guidance and never infer a current default or downgrade from an unverified snapshot.

strengths: Requires current official sources and preserves explicit model targets.
